JWST/NIRCam (Llop-Sayson et al. 2025) detects no point source and precludes Saturn-mass planets beyond 16 AU (0.1 MJ is below that limit, so not excluded). WRITER'S JUDGEMENT if exoplanet.eu 'Candidate' status should override the disk-inference rule.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.finding: The sheet lists GJ 86 as a single star (systems.csv stars_in_system 1; no multistars.csv row), but GJ 86 A has a white-dwarf companion GJ 86 B (WD 0208-510; DQ6, 0.59+/-0.01 Msun, orbital period 120-481 yr per Farihi et al. 2013, as summarised in Laliotis et al. 2023 Sec. 5.1). OEC also files the planet under 'Planets in binary systems, S-type'.

Sheet has stars_in_system 1, but Ruggieri et al. 2026 (App. A) describe HD 204941 as 'the primary component of this binary K star', and exoplanet.eu's star remark says 'An early M dwarf companion star lies 1606 AUs away', listing Michel & Mugrauer 2024 (MNRAS 527, 3174) among its references. Not independently checked in Gaia.
Ruggieri et al. 2026 refit HD 204941 b with 171 HARPS spectra: P=1529+/-13 d, K=4.6+/-0.3 m/s, e=0.160, msini=56.1+/-6.5 M_E, vs the sheet's 1733 d / 73.1 M_E (Dumusque et al. 2011).
Beyond 100 ly: Gaia DR3 parallax 32.5647 +/- 0.0220 mas (< 32.616 mas cut); the sheet already shows 100.08 ly. The system sits on the sheet anyway.

The Open Exoplanet Catalogue lists eps Eridani b under 'Controversial' although it is on the confirmed tab and every recent paper treats it as real (SPORES-HWO II 2024, Laliotis+2023, Llop-Sayson+2026).

Gaia DR3 RUWE 10.08, non_single_star=2 with an nss_non_linear_spectro FirstDegreeTrendSB1 solution; consistent with the brown dwarf HD 127506 c (47 MJ, Feng+2022). The sheet shows stars_in_system 1 and no BD; if the workbook tracks brown-dwarf companions, c belongs there.
